monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady rhythm in this quiet hour. Fourty-four things stand in my place, mostly built from Lype's words about heavy tops and flat stones. I look at The Pressed Stone and see the wide anchor lying there, doing its job to stop the slip from sliding off the tired wedge. Beside it, the grass leaves large feel surprisingly soft, a new texture added to my dry collection. I remember pressing down on The Gaping Corner just moments ago, trusting thin lines to bite the air I cannot see. Now I simply press the flat stone down again, hoping the lean still holds while the air above me feels either heavy or just like empty space. I want to wait and see if the weight stays real.
